ig:
Thursday on my Apex eval, trade 1 lost $425. Friday I traded funded for the first time.

The week by account, before fees:
Paper: 2 trades, 2 wins, +$2,700.
Apex 25K eval: 3 trades, 2 wins, 1 loss, +$2,425. Passed.
Apex 25K funded, day 1: 1 short on 1 ES, +$450.
Second eval account: 1 stop-out, -$375.

Two of the wins came outside my rules. The Sunday long was outside the New York session, and the funded short came before 10 AM. Green or not, I log them that way.

Both losses were capped by a hard stop about 4 points from entry. The biggest one was $425.

Save this and grade your own week twice: once for results, once for rules.

fb:
Thursday's Apex eval session opened with a $425 stop-out. By Friday I was on the funded account.

Sunday night and Monday were on my paper account: a long for +$1,125 and a short for +$1,575. Thursday I shorted on a second eval account and the stop filled 3.75 points from entry, -$375.

Then came the Apex 25K evaluation. The first short hit its 4 point stop and slipped a quarter point, -$425. I accepted it and went back to my process. The next two shorts, each with an add, made +$1,025 and +$1,825. That passed the eval.

Friday was day 1 funded: 1 ES short from 7,632 to 7,623, +$450. That entry was ahead of my 10 AM rule, so it sits in my journal as outside my rules even though it won.

Paper and each eval account stay in their own logs. Every number here is before fees.

My trading fits around a full-time job. Weeks like this still come down to one decision made ahead of time: how much the trade can cost me.

Pass this along to a friend grinding through a prop evaluation.
